findings.description: All findings of the event with their final state. Required in the full profile (rule R10); in minimized it may be omitted and the metric counts stand.

residue.description: The heart of the declaration (section 6): what the cycle could not close by itself, in three classes, or the express declaration of absence. Common to the three classes: none was backed by execution; they rest on someone's judgment.

declared_absence.description: Only if no residue remained. Absence is declared expressly, never left implicit in an empty field (section 12.2, failure 2).

declaration.description: Text of the express declaration of absence. Rule R2 of the validator rejects generic markers (N/A, none, all resolved, applied). Honest limit of the control: the machine detects the empty field and the generic marker, not the false declaration; human sampling remains the only real defense against cosmetic compliance.

text.description: Quote of code, contractual data or observable behavior. Full profile only.

link.description: Stable reference (permalink to a line, test, log).

hash.description: Hash of the evidence. Only content admitted in the minimized profile.

origin.description: reviewer_id of the reviewer that produced it.

location.description: Path and affected lines. Full profile only.

final_state.description: Terminal outcome of the finding at the close of the event. The first three are the three forms of a valid finding (section 11). The two refuted ones are false positives; the interpretive one additionally joins the residue. escalated_open joins the residue and counts in no numerator.

against.description: What the generator checked the finding against before accepting or refuting it (do not blindly trust the reviewer; decorrelation goes both ways). repository: code, config, contracts. execution: running tests or the program. external_source: literature, third-party specifications, advisories or external documentation. none: no verification was performed.

remedy_adjustment.description: When the finding is valid but the remedy proposed by the reviewer was wrong and it was adopted with modification. The finding counts as incorporated; the adjustment is recorded.

fix_verification.description: An incorporated finding does not close when the fix is applied but when the fix passed its own verification: a diff gate over that change or a specific test (section 6). Required in the diff gate for the incorporated state (rule R7).

debt_id.description: Required if final_state = debt_recorded: identifier in the technical debt system.

risk_record.description: Required if final_state = owner_decision: record of the accepted risk or the scope change.

class.description: The three classes of section 6 plus the two the degraded modes of v0.4 introduce: reviewer_correlation, the errors a reviewer shares with the generator because it was not from another family, and reviewer_hardening_gap, the possibility that the reviewed material addressed the reviewer.

finding_ref.description: Originating finding, if applicable. execution_gap items may not be born from a finding.

requires_human_attention.description: true at minimum for every interpretive refutation: it is the one that asks for human attention (section 6).

refutation_type.description: Required if class = principal_refutation. Verifiable: quote of code, contractual data or observable behavior. Interpretive: domain or architecture judgment. Both are declared so the human reviewer can decline to take them at face value.

lead_acceptance.description: In Level A, an execution gap blocks the merge until a technical lead accepts it in writing (section 7). Rule R5 enforces it.

record.description: Link or identifier of the written record of the acceptance.

reviewer_ref.description: reviewer_id this item is about. Required for the two reviewer classes: one item cannot cover several degraded reviewers, or the record stops saying which one carried the risk.

allOf.$comment: v0.3 hardening. Conditioned on the declared version so that reading a historical v0.2 declaration never requires rewriting it: what a PR may ADD is governed by the gate.

A verifiable refutation closes a finding without touching the code: it demands material evidence, not merely the presence of the object, and a verifiable target. A blank string is presence, not material: text and link must carry a non-whitespace character.
